rules.title: California Statewide Rent Cap (AB 1482 / Civ. Code § 1947.12)
rules.requirement: Landlords cannot raise rent on covered residential units by more than 5% plus local CPI change, or 10%, whichever is lower, in any 12-month period, and no more than two increases in that period.
rules.key_value: 5% + CPI, max 10%
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to residential real property generally, subject to listed exemptions (deed-restricted affordable housing, dorms/schools, locally rent-controlled housing with stricter caps, housing with certificate of occupancy within prior 15 years, certain owner-occupied duplexes, and certain non-corporate single-family/condo owners with required notice).
rules.exemptions: Deed-restricted affordable housing; dormitories; housing subject to stricter local rent control; housing issued certificate of occupancy within previous 15 years (unless mobilehome); alienable single-family/condo property owned by a non-REIT/non-corporation/non-LLC-with-corporate-member with required tenant notice; owner-occupied duplexes where owner occupies one unit.
rules.interaction: Does not apply to units covered by a more protective local rent control ordinance, such as those in Berkeley, San Francisco, Los Angeles, and Santa Ana.
rules.quoted_span: an owner of residential real property shall not, over the course of any 12-month period, increase the gross rental rate for a dwelling or a unit more than 5 percent plus the percentage change in the cost of living, or 10 percent, whichever is lower, of the lowest gross rental rate charged for that dwelling or unit at any time during the 12 months prior to the effective date of the increase.
rules.conflict_note: Operative date differs from original enactment (Jan 1, 2020); section is repealed as of Jan 1, 2030.

coverage.other_unknown_factor: whether the unit is deed-restricted/subsidized affordable housing; whether the owner is a natural person/non-corporate entity for single-family/condo exemption; whether tenant received required statutory notice of exemption

rules.effective_date_note: Annual recalculation of existing rent cap formula under AB 1482
rules.title_es: Límite estatal de aumento de renta en California (AB 1482 / Código Civil § 1947.12)
rules.requirement_es: Los arrendadores no pueden aumentar la renta de las unidades residenciales cubiertas más del 5% más el cambio del IPC local, o el 10%, lo que sea menor, en cualquier período de 12 meses, y no se permiten más de dos aumentos en ese período.
rules.key_value_es: 5% + IPC, máximo 10%

rules.title: California Tenant Protection Act – Just Cause for Termination of Tenancy
rules.requirement: Once all tenants have lawfully occupied a rental unit for 12 months (or at least one tenant for 24 months), a landlord must state a just cause in any notice to terminate the tenancy, and failure to comply voids the termination notice. This rule does not apply where a local just-cause ordinance adopted on or before September 1, 2019, or a more protective local ordinance adopted after that date, governs instead.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to residential real property (dwellings/units intended for human habitation, including mobilehome park units) once tenants have met the 12/24-month occupancy threshold; does not apply where a qualifying local just-cause ordinance applies instead.
rules.exemptions: Does not apply to residential real property subject to a local just-cause ordinance adopted on or before September 1, 2019 (local ordinance governs), or to a more protective local ordinance adopted/amended after that date meeting specified criteria; does not apply to a homeowner of a mobilehome as defined in Section 798.9.
rules.interaction: Does not apply where a local just-cause ordinance adopted on or before Sept 1, 2019 (or a more protective later one) governs instead, e.g., in Berkeley, San Francisco, Los Angeles, San Diego, and Santa Ana.
rules.quoted_span: (A) Residential real property subject to a local ordinance requiring just cause for termination of a residential tenancy adopted on or before September 1, 2019, in which case the local ordinance shall apply.
rules.conflict_note: Underlying section originally effective 2020-01-01; the version addressing interaction with local ordinances became operative 2024-04-01; a later amendment is effective 2026-01-01; the section is set to self-repeal 2030-01-01.

coverage.other_unknown_factor: whether a local just-cause eviction ordinance (adopted on or before Sept 1, 2019, or a later ordinance found to be more protective) governs the property instead of this section

rules.effective_date_note: Established tenant protection law, this date reflects continuing statutory provision/exception
rules.title_es: Ley de Protección al Inquilino de California – Causa justa para terminar el arrendamiento
rules.requirement_es: Una vez que todos los inquilinos hayan ocupado legalmente una unidad de alquiler durante 12 meses (o al menos un inquilino durante 24 meses), el arrendador debe indicar una causa justa en cualquier aviso de terminación del contrato, y el incumplimiento de esto anula el aviso de terminación. Esta regla no aplica cuando una ordenanza local de causa justa adoptada el 1 de septiembre de 2019 o antes, o una ordenanza local más protectora adoptada después de esa fecha, regula en su lugar.

rules.title: Security Deposit Limits (Civil Code § 1950.5)
rules.requirement: Landlords generally may not demand a security deposit of more than one month's rent (on top of the first month's rent). Small landlords who are natural persons and own no more than two rental properties totaling four units or fewer may charge up to two months' rent as security, except this higher amount cannot be charged to a service member.
rules.key_value: 1 month's rent cap; 2 months' rent for small landlords (natural person owning ≤2 properties/≤4 units)
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to security charged for residential rental agreements where the property is used as the tenant's dwelling.
rules.exemptions: Advance payment of not less than six months' rent allowed if lease term is six months or longer; small landlord exception for natural persons/LLCs of natural persons owning ≤2 properties totaling ≤4 units (does not apply to service members); exception does not apply to security collected before July 1, 2024.
rules.interaction: Local ordinances (e.g., Berkeley) may add additional requirements such as interest payment on deposits, supplementing but not conflicting with this state cap.
rules.quoted_span: a landlord shall not demand or receive security, however denominated, in an amount or value in excess of an amount equal to one month’s rent, in addition to any rent for the first month paid on or before initial occupancy.
rules.conflict_note: Deposit-amount cap effective 2024-07-01 (AB 12); separate itemization/nonrefundable provisions amended by AB 414 effective 2026-01-01.

coverage.other_unknown_factor: whether the tenant is a service member, which affects allowable deposit amount and disclosure requirements

rules.effective_date_note: Amendment lowering/adjusting existing deposit cap rules with new small-landlord carveout
rules.title_es: Límites del depósito de seguridad (Código Civil § 1950.5)
rules.requirement_es: Por lo general, los arrendadores no pueden exigir un depósito de seguridad de más de un mes de renta (además del primer mes de renta). Los pequeños propietarios que sean personas naturales y posean no más de dos propiedades de alquiler con un total de cuatro unidades o menos pueden cobrar hasta dos meses de renta como depósito, excepto que este monto mayor no se puede cobrar a un miembro del servicio militar.
rules.key_value_es: Límite de 1 mes de renta; 2 meses de renta para pequeños propietarios (persona natural con ≤2 propiedades/≤4 unidades)

rules.title: Application Screening Fee Cap
rules.requirement: Landlords can charge a fee to cover the cost of screening a rental applicant, but the fee cannot exceed actual out-of-pocket costs and is capped at $30 per applicant (adjustable for inflation). Landlords must follow specific procedures for considering applications in order and refunding fees when applicants are not considered, and must provide an itemized receipt.
rules.key_value: $30 per applicant (CPI-adjusted since 1998)
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to all landlords charging an application screening fee to a rental applicant in California.
rules.interaction: Applies statewide; local ordinances such as Berkeley's require disclosure of this cap but cannot set a different cap amount.
rules.quoted_span: In no case shall the amount of the application screening fee charged by the landlord or their agent be greater than thirty dollars ($30) per applicant. The thirty dollar ($30) application screening fee may be adjusted annually by the landlord or their agent commensurate with an increase in the Consumer Price Index, beginning on January 1, 1998.
rules.conflict_note: Base cap is $30 (1998), CPI-adjusted annually; the 2026 cap is $68.96.
rules.effective_date_note: Existing screening fee cap adjusted for inflation
rules.title_es: Límite de la tarifa de investigación de solicitud
rules.requirement_es: Los arrendadores pueden cobrar una tarifa para cubrir el costo de investigar a un solicitante de alquiler, pero la tarifa no puede exceder los costos reales de bolsillo y tiene un tope de $30 por solicitante (ajustable por inflación). Los arrendadores deben seguir procedimientos específicos para considerar las solicitudes en orden y reembolsar las tarifas cuando los solicitantes no sean considerados, y deben proporcionar un recibo detallado.
rules.key_value_es: $30 por solicitante (ajustado por IPC desde 1998)

rules.title: Civil Rights Council criminal history screening regulations
rules.requirement: Landlords face strict limits on how they can use an applicant's criminal history, including a ban on blanket bans on applicants with a criminal record and a ban on considering arrests that did not lead to conviction.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to landlords conducting criminal background checks on rental applicants in California.
rules.interaction: Berkeley's Fair Chance Access to Housing Ordinance imposes a stricter, near-total ban on criminal history inquiries beyond this state regulation's limits.
rules.citation: Cal. Code Regs. tit. 2 (Civil Rights Council Criminal History Regulations); Cal. Gov. Code § 12955
rules.quoted_span: Blanket bans on applicants with a criminal record are prohibited, as are policies that consider arrests without convictions.
rules.conflict_note: One source lacks a specific statutory/regulatory citation and infers authority from general FEHA; exact regulatory citation is uncertain across sources.
rules.effective_date_note: New regulatory restrictions on criminal history screening
rules.title_es: Reglamentos del Consejo de Derechos Civiles sobre investigación de antecedentes penales
rules.requirement_es: Los arrendadores enfrentan límites estrictos sobre cómo pueden usar los antecedentes penales de un solicitante, incluyendo la prohibición de rechazos generales a solicitantes con antecedentes penales y la prohibición de considerar arrestos que no resultaron en condena.

rules.title: California Fair Employment and Housing Act - Housing Discrimination (Source of Income / Credit History)
rules.requirement: Landlords cannot refuse to rent to tenants because they pay with a housing voucher or other lawful source of income, and where a tenant has a government rent subsidy, the landlord must let the applicant offer alternative proof of ability to pay (like pay stubs or bank statements) instead of relying solely on credit history.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to owners of housing accommodations in California; special credit-history alternative-evidence rule applies specifically where there is a government rent subsidy involved.
rules.interaction: Applies statewide to all landlords regardless of local ordinances; no local override identified.
rules.quoted_span: For the owner of any housing accommodation to discriminate against or harass any person because of the race, color, religion, sex, gender, gender identity, gender expression, sexual orientation, marital status, national origin, ancestry, familial status, source of income, disability, veteran or military status, or genetic information of that person.
rules.conflict_note: SB 329 (effective 2020-01-01) established source-of-income protections; a later amendment described in one source (effective 2024-01-01) added a requirement to accept alternative income proof for subsidized tenants; sources cite different effective dates for different amendments to the same code section.

coverage.other_unknown_factor: whether a government rent subsidy (e.g., Section 8 voucher) applies to the tenancy

rules.effective_date_note: Longstanding FEHA anti-discrimination provisions
rules.title_es: Ley de Vivienda Justa y Empleo Justo de California - Discriminación por vivienda (fuente de ingresos / historial crediticio)
rules.requirement_es: Los arrendadores no pueden negarse a alquilar a inquilinos porque paguen con un vale de vivienda u otra fuente legal de ingresos, y cuando un inquilino tenga un subsidio de renta del gobierno, el arrendador debe permitir que el solicitante ofrezca prueba alternativa de capacidad de pago (como recibos de sueldo o estados de cuenta bancarios) en lugar de basarse únicamente en el historial crediticio.

rules.title: SB 267 - Credit history restriction for voucher holders
rules.requirement: Landlords may not use an applicant's credit history as part of the application process if the applicant has a government rental subsidy (like Section 8), unless they offer the applicant a chance to provide alternative proof they can pay their share of rent.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to rental property owners screening applicants who hold a government rental subsidy.
rules.quoted_span:
In addition, last year’s
SB 267 amended FEHA
to prohibit rental property owners from using a person’s credit history as part of the application process – if they have a government rental subsidy, such as Section 8 — without offering the applicant the option to provide alternative evidence of a verifiable legal means to pay their portion of the rent.
rules.conflict_note: Effective date not stated in source; SB 267 was enacted in 2023, presumed effective 2024-01-01.
rules.title_es: SB 267 - Restricción del historial crediticio para titulares de vales
rules.requirement_es: Los arrendadores no pueden usar el historial crediticio de un solicitante como parte del proceso de solicitud si el solicitante tiene un subsidio de alquiler del gobierno (como la Sección 8), a menos que le ofrezcan al solicitante la oportunidad de proporcionar una prueba alternativa de que puede pagar su parte de la renta.

rules.title: AB-325 Cartwright Act: violations (common pricing algorithm ban)
rules.requirement: It is illegal to use or distribute a common pricing algorithm that coordinates pricing among competitors or coerces someone to adopt a price or term recommended by such an algorithm, including for rental housing or other products/services.
rules.key_value: Ban on use/distribution of common pricing algorithms for coordinated or coerced pricing
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to any person using or distributing a common pricing algorithm as part of a contract, combination, or conspiracy to restrain trade, or who coerces another to adopt an algorithm-recommended price or term, for products or services in California.
rules.exemptions: Does not impair or limit applicability of other antitrust laws; 'person' does not include the end consumer.
rules.interaction: Operates alongside (not preempting) local algorithmic rent-setting bans in Berkeley, San Diego, and Santa Ana, which add housing-specific penalties and private rights of action.
rules.quoted_span: It shall be unlawful for a person to use or distribute a common pricing algorithm as part of a contract, combination in the form of a trust, or conspiracy to restrain trade or commerce in violation of this chapter.
rules.conflict_note: No explicit effective date in statutory text; California bills without urgency clauses typically take effect Jan 1 following enactment, consistent with a secondary source's stated 2026-01-01 date.

coverage.other_unknown_factor: Whether the business uses a 'common' algorithm (shared by multiple users and incorporating competitor data) versus a proprietary single-firm algorithm

rules.effective_date_note: Newly enacted ban on algorithmic pricing
rules.title_es: AB-325 Ley Cartwright: infracciones (prohibición de algoritmos comunes de fijación de precios)
rules.requirement_es: Es ilegal usar o distribuir un algoritmo común de fijación de precios que coordine precios entre competidores o coaccione a alguien a adoptar un precio o término recomendado por dicho algoritmo, incluso para vivienda de alquiler u otros productos/servicios.
rules.key_value_es: Prohibición de uso/distribución de algoritmos comunes de fijación de precios para coordinar o coaccionar precios

rules.title: 2026 Annual General Adjustment (AGA) Order
rules.requirement: Berkeley landlords with rent-controlled units may increase the 2025 permanent rent ceiling by 1.0%, but not before January 1, 2026. This increase does not apply to tenancies that began on or after January 1, 2025 and whose rents were set under the Costa-Hawkins Rental Housing Act.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to units subject to Berkeley rent stabilization with permanent rent ceilings; excludes tenancies beginning on or after January 1, 2025 whose rents were set under Costa-Hawkins (i.e., units exempt from rent ceiling because of vacancy decontrol).
rules.exemptions: Tenancies that began on or after January 1, 2025 and had rents set pursuant to the Costa-Hawkins Rental Housing Act are not subject to this AGA increase.
rules.interaction: The state AB 1482 rent cap does not apply to units covered by Berkeley's local rent control ordinance, which imposes its own stricter annual cap.
rules.quoted_span:
At its regular meeting on October 16, 2025, the Berkeley Rent Stabilization Board 
adopted the Annual General Adjustment (AGA) Order for Year 2026 which will allow 
eligible landlords to increase the 2025 permanent rent ceilings by 1.0% no earlier than 
January 1, 2026.
rules.conflict_note: Measure BB (Nov 2024) capped the Annual General Adjustment formula at 5%; the 2026 Rent Board order sets the actual AGA at 1.0%, both under the same ch. 13.76 regime.

coverage.other_unknown_factor: whether the unit's rent is subject to a permanent rent ceiling under Berkeley rent stabilization or instead set under Costa-Hawkins vacancy decontrol (tenancy began on or after Jan 1, 2025)

rules.effective_date_note: Annual adjustment of existing rent ceiling program
rules.title_es: Orden de Ajuste General Anual (AGA) 2026
rules.requirement_es: Los arrendadores de Berkeley con unidades bajo control de renta pueden aumentar el techo de renta permanente de 2025 en un 1.0%, pero no antes del 1 de enero de 2026. Este aumento no aplica a arrendamientos que comenzaron el 1 de enero de 2025 o después y cuyas rentas se establecieron bajo la Ley Costa-Hawkins de Vivienda de Alquiler.

rules.title: Measure BB - Just Cause Eviction Changes (Nonpayment Threshold, Lease Breach, Notice Requirements)
rules.requirement: In Berkeley, tenants in covered units cannot be evicted for nonpayment of rent unless they owe at least one month's Fair Market Rent for an equivalent-size unit; landlords can no longer evict for failing to sign a new fixed-term lease; eviction for lease-breach requires that the breach actually harm the landlord and that tenant behavior be shown to be unreasonable; and termination notices must direct tenants to the Rent Board and be filed with the Rent Board within three business days of service.
rules.key_value: Nonpayment eviction threshold: 1 month's Fair Market Rent (FMR)
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to tenants in units that are fully or partially covered by Berkeley's Rent Ordinance.
rules.exemptions: Units exempt from the Rent Ordinance (e.g., certain new construction, most single-family homes/condos, certain federally subsidized units) are not covered by these just-cause protections.
rules.interaction: Because this is a local just-cause ordinance adopted before Sept 1, 2019, it displaces the default state just-cause requirement under Civ. Code §1946.2 for covered Berkeley units.
rules.quoted_span: For a landlord to evict a tenant for nonpayment of rent, the tenant must owe an amount of rental debt equal to or greater than one month of the Fair Market Rent (FMR) value for a unit of equivalent size in the metro area Oakland-Fremont, CA HUD Metro FMR as determined by the US Department of Housing and Urban Development for the fiscal year in which the rent is demanded.
rules.conflict_note: Sources give different effective dates for different components (e.g., relocation payment increases effective 2026-01-01; Measure BB passed the Nov 2024 election without one stated effective date for the nonpayment threshold change).

coverage.other_unknown_factor: Whether the unit is government-owned/subsidized and whether tenant shares kitchen/bath with a landlord who resided there first (affects exemption status).

rules.title_es: Medida BB - Cambios en el desalojo por causa justa (umbral de falta de pago, incumplimiento de contrato, requisitos de notificación)
rules.requirement_es: En Berkeley, los inquilinos en unidades cubiertas no pueden ser desalojados por falta de pago de renta a menos que deban al menos un mes de la Renta de Mercado Justa (FMR) para una unidad de tamaño equivalente; los arrendadores ya no pueden desalojar por no firmar un nuevo contrato de plazo fijo; el desalojo por incumplimiento del contrato requiere que el incumplimiento realmente perjudique al arrendador y que se demuestre que el comportamiento del inquilino fue irrazonable; y los avisos de terminación deben dirigir a los inquilinos a la Junta de Renta y deben presentarse ante la Junta de Renta dentro de tres días hábiles de la notificación.
rules.key_value_es: Umbral de desalojo por falta de pago: 1 mes de la Renta de Mercado Justa (FMR)

rules.title: Berkeley Security Deposit Interest Requirement
rules.requirement: For tenancies in units fully or partially covered by Berkeley's Rent Ordinance, landlords must pay tenants interest on their security deposit at the end of each year, with a prorated amount if the tenant moves out before year-end.
rules.key_value: Annual interest on security deposit
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to units fully or partially covered by Berkeley's Rent Ordinance.
rules.interaction: Supplements the state deposit cap (Civ. Code §1950.5) by requiring interest payments on deposits for rent-controlled units.
rules.quoted_span: For tenancies in units fully or partially covered by Berkeley's Rent Ordinance, landlords must pay tenants interest on their security deposit at the end of each year and a prorated amount if the tenant moves out before the end of the year.

coverage.other_unknown_factor: whether the unit is fully or partially covered by Berkeley's Rent Ordinance

rules.title_es: Requisito de interés sobre depósito de seguridad en Berkeley
rules.requirement_es: Para los arrendamientos en unidades total o parcialmente cubiertas por la Ordenanza de Renta de Berkeley, los arrendadores deben pagar a los inquilinos intereses sobre su depósito de seguridad al final de cada año, con un monto prorrateado si el inquilino se muda antes de que termine el año.
rules.key_value_es: Interés anual sobre el depósito de seguridad

rules.title: Notification of State Law Limitation on Tenant Screening Fees
rules.requirement: Before charging a screening fee, a Berkeley landlord must give applicants a clear statement of their tenant screening fee rights and the state maximum fee cap.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies when an owner or agent charges a fee to purchase a consumer credit report or process a rental application in Berkeley.
rules.interaction: Works alongside the state screening-fee cap under Civ. Code §1950.6; requires disclosure of the state cap and adds a separate local prohibition on non-refundable renewal/roommate fees.
rules.quoted_span:
the owner must provide, either in the rental application or in a separate disclosure before receiving the fee, a clear and conspicuous tenant screening fee rights statement and a statement of the maximum fee cap permitted under
California Civil Code Section 1950.6(b)
rules.title_es: Notificación de la limitación estatal sobre las tarifas de investigación de inquilinos
rules.requirement_es: Antes de cobrar una tarifa de investigación, un arrendador de Berkeley debe entregar a los solicitantes una declaración clara de sus derechos respecto a la tarifa de investigación de inquilinos y el tope máximo estatal de la tarifa.

rules.title: Ronald V. Dellums Fair Chance Access to Housing Ordinance
rules.requirement: Berkeley landlords cannot ask about or use criminal history in advertising, applications, tenant selection, or decisions about renting, and cannot charge higher deposits or rent based on criminal history.
rules.key_value: Ban on criminal history inquiries/use in housing decisions
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to rental housing providers in Berkeley for current or prospective tenants, with listed exemptions.
rules.exemptions: Lifetime sex offenders; public housing/Section 8 properties (limited exemptions); owner-occupied properties (1-3 units) where an owner resides as primary residence; units under agreement allowing owner to move back in; units occupied by existing tenants seeking to sublet or add/replace roommates.
rules.interaction: State law (Gov. Code §12955/Civil Rights Council regs) restricts but does not entirely bar use of criminal history; Berkeley's ordinance imposes a stricter, near-total local ban.
rules.quoted_span: The Fair Chance Access to Housing Ordinance prohibits rental housing providers in Berkeley from asking about and using criminal history and/or criminal background checks in their rental housing advertising, applications, tenant selection process, or decision-making.

coverage.other_unknown_factor: whether the applicant is a lifetime sex offender, whether the unit is public housing/Section 8, or whether the unit is occupied by existing tenants seeking to sublet or add/replace roommates

rules.title_es: Ordenanza Ronald V. Dellums de Acceso Justo a la Vivienda
rules.requirement_es: Los arrendadores de Berkeley no pueden preguntar sobre ni usar los antecedentes penales en publicidad, solicitudes, selección de inquilinos o decisiones sobre el alquiler, y no pueden cobrar depósitos o rentas más altos basados en los antecedentes penales.
rules.key_value_es: Prohibición de preguntas/uso de antecedentes penales en decisiones de vivienda

rules.title: Prohibition on the Sale or Use of Coordinated Pricing Algorithms to Set Rents or Manage Occupancy Levels for Residential Dwelling Units
rules.requirement: Landlords in Berkeley may not use, and companies may not sell or provide, software that uses nonpublic competitor data to coordinate rent or occupancy level recommendations between competing landlords for residential units.
rules.key_value: Ban on use/sale of coordinated pricing algorithms; penalties up to $1,000 per violation
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to all residential dwelling units in the City of Berkeley; covers any landlord using or any vendor selling a 'coordinated pricing algorithm' as defined, using non-public competitor data less than 90 days old.
rules.exemptions: Does not cover aggregated/anonymized public data reports, affordable housing rent/income-limit setting products, market research for project financing, appraisals, or research/testing/training of software models where competitor data is not used as a live input.
rules.interaction: Overlaps with the CA Cartwright Act (Bus. & Prof. Code §16729) banning algorithmic pricing collusion statewide; the local ordinance adds city-specific civil penalties and a private right of action.
rules.quoted_span:
It shall be unlawful to sell, license, or otherwise provide to City of Berkeley 
landlords any coordinated pricing algorithm that sets or recommends rents or occupancy 
levels that may be achieved for residential dwelling units in the City of Berkeley.
rules.conflict_note: Official ordinance text does not state a separate effective date beyond Council passage (Nov 18, 2025); a secondary source estimates an effective date of January 2026.

coverage.other_unknown_factor: whether the landlord uses or sells a coordinated pricing algorithm incorporating nonpublic competitor data less than 90 days old, or whether the product falls within an exempted use (aggregated public data, affordable housing limits, appraisal/research use)

rules.effective_date_note: New first-ever ban on coordinated pricing algorithms
rules.title_es: Prohibición de la venta o uso de algoritmos de fijación de precios coordinados para establecer rentas o gestionar niveles de ocupación en unidades residenciales
rules.requirement_es: Los arrendadores en Berkeley no pueden usar, y las empresas no pueden vender ni proporcionar, software que use datos no públicos de competidores para coordinar recomendaciones de renta o nivel de ocupación entre arrendadores competidores de unidades residenciales.
rules.key_value_es: Prohibición del uso/venta de algoritmos de fijación de precios coordinados; sanciones de hasta $1,000 por infracción

rules.title: RSO Annual Rent Increase Cap
rules.requirement: For rental units covered by the Los Angeles Rent Stabilization Ordinance, landlords may raise rent by at most the annual allowable percentage set by the city, currently 3%, plus certain fee surcharges.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to rental units subject to the City of Los Angeles Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO).
rules.exemptions: Non-RSO properties are not covered by this cap.
rules.interaction: The state AB 1482 rent cap does not apply to units covered by this local RSO, which has its own stricter annual cap and separate fee surcharges.
rules.quoted_span:
Annual rent increases for rental units subject to the City of Los Angeles Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO), effective
July 1, 2025, through June 30, 2026
is
3%
rules.conflict_note: Annual allowable percentage changes each year (3% for 7/1/2025-6/30/2026); separate surcharge pass-throughs (RSO/SCEP fees) have different effective dates (2020, 2022).

coverage.other_unknown_factor: whether the unit is registered as subject to the RSO (determined via zimas.lacity.org lookup)

rules.effective_date_note: Annual update of existing RSO rent increase cap
rules.title_es: Tope anual de aumento de renta de la RSO
rules.requirement_es: Para las unidades de alquiler cubiertas por la Ordenanza de Estabilización de Renta de Los Ángeles, los arrendadores pueden aumentar la renta como máximo el porcentaje anual permitido establecido por la ciudad, actualmente 3%, más ciertos recargos de tarifas.

rules.title: RSO Legal Reasons for Eviction & Notice Filing
rules.requirement: Landlords of RSO-covered units may only evict tenants for specified at-fault or no-fault reasons, and all termination notices must be filed with LAHD within three business days of service on the tenant.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to rental units subject to the City's Rent Stabilization Ordinance.
rules.interaction: As a local just-cause ordinance adopted before Sept 1, 2019, this ordinance displaces the state Tenant Protection Act default; where state Housing Crisis Act relocation requirements exceed local RSO/JCO amounts, landlords must pay the higher amount.
rules.quoted_span:
ll notices to terminate a tenancy for all rental units subject to
City’s Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO
) must be filed with the Los Angeles Housing Department (LAHD) within
three (3) business days of service on the tenant
per Los Angeles Municipal Code 151.09.C.9 & 165.05.B.5.
rules.conflict_note: Relocation assistance amounts vary annually (current figures for 7/1/2026-6/30/2027) and overlap with state Housing Crisis Act requirements, which may require higher payments for lower-income tenants displaced for new construction (Resident Protections Ordinance, effective 2025-02-11).

coverage.other_unknown_factor: Whether the tenant is 'eligible' or 'qualified' (age, disability, dependents) and whether the tenant is low-income, which affect the relocation amount owed; whether the property is a single-family dwelling owned by a natural person owning 4 or fewer units.

rules.title_es: Motivos legales de desalojo según la RSO y presentación de avisos
rules.requirement_es: Los arrendadores de unidades cubiertas por la RSO solo pueden desalojar a los inquilinos por motivos específicos con o sin culpa, y todos los avisos de terminación deben presentarse ante el LAHD dentro de tres días hábiles de haber sido notificados al inquilino.

rules.title: Prohibited Activities - Source of Income Discrimination
rules.requirement: Landlords in Los Angeles cannot refuse to rent, apply different terms, misrepresent availability, or advertise preferences based on a prospective or current tenant's source of income, including housing vouchers.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to any person offering for rent, renting, or listing a housing accommodation in Los Angeles.
rules.interaction: Supplements state FEHA source-of-income protections with city-specific anti-discrimination enforcement provisions.
rules.quoted_span: Based upon a person’s source of income, refuse to rent or lease, or to continue to rent or lease, a housing accommodation; refuse to enter into or renew a rental agreement, lease or housing assistance payment contract
rules.title_es: Actividades prohibidas - Discriminación por fuente de ingresos
rules.requirement_es: Los arrendadores en Los Ángeles no pueden negarse a alquilar, aplicar términos diferentes, tergiversar la disponibilidad ni anunciar preferencias basadas en la fuente de ingresos de un inquilino actual o potencial, incluidos los vales de vivienda.

rules.title: Just Cause Required for Termination of Tenancy
rules.requirement: Landlords in San Diego generally cannot end a tenancy without a legally listed 'just cause' reason, either tenant-at-fault (like nonpayment of rent or lease violation) or no-fault (like owner move-in, demolition, or substantial remodel), and many no-fault reasons require relocation assistance to the tenant.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to most residential rental properties/tenancies in San Diego of more than 30 days duration, subject to listed exemptions (e.g., single-family owner-occupied homes, duplexes with owner occupying one unit, deed-restricted affordable housing, properties issued a certificate of occupancy within the previous 15 years, and certain non-corporate-owned alienable properties with required tenant notice).
rules.exemptions: Transient/tourist hotel occupancy; short-term residential occupancy; deed-restricted affordable housing (with Section 8 carve-out); mobilehomes under Mobilehome Residency Law; nonprofit/religious/care facility housing; school dormitories; shared-facility tenancies with resident landlord; owner-occupied single-family residences (with limited rentable rooms/ADUs); duplexes where landlord occupies one unit; housing issued a certificate of occupancy within the previous 15 years (unless a mobilehome); and certain alienable properties not owned by a REIT, corporation, or corporate-member LLC, with required tenant notice.
rules.interaction: Operates alongside and consistent with the state Tenant Protection Act (Civ. Code §1946.2), adding local relocation assistance and buyout protections; as a local just-cause ordinance it displaces the default state rule for covered units.
rules.quoted_span:
A landlord shall not terminate a tenancy without just cause. For purposes of this 
Division, just cause includes at-fault just cause and no-fault just cause.
rules.conflict_note: Section 98.0706 was amended 2024-02-27 (effective 2024-03-28); the original ordinance was effective 2023-06-24.

coverage.other_unknown_factor: whether the housing is deed-restricted/subsidized affordable housing; whether the landlord is a REIT, corporation, or LLC with a corporate member (for the alienable-property exemption); whether the tenant shares bathroom/kitchen facilities with a resident landlord

rules.title_es: Se requiere causa justa para la terminación del arrendamiento
rules.requirement_es: Los arrendadores en San Diego generalmente no pueden poner fin a un arrendamiento sin una 'causa justa' listada legalmente, ya sea por culpa del inquilino (como falta de pago de renta o violación del contrato) o sin culpa (como mudanza del propietario, demolición o remodelación sustancial), y muchos motivos sin culpa requieren asistencia de reubicación al inquilino.

rules.title: Use and Sale of Algorithmic Devices Prohibited
rules.requirement: Landlords cannot use algorithmic software to set rental rates or occupancy levels for residential rental property, and no one may sell or provide such algorithmic devices to landlords. Tenants can sue for damages, injunctive relief, or civil penalties up to $1,000 per violation.
rules.key_value: Up to $1,000 per violation
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to landlords and residential rental property as defined in San Diego Municipal Code section 98.0702; excludes software used only to publish aggregated historical (90+ days old) or publicly available data without recommending future rates, and software used to set rates per affordable housing program guidelines.
rules.exemptions: Software reporting only aggregated historical nonpublic competitor data older than 90 days or public data without future rate recommendations; software used to establish rates/income limits per affordable housing program guidelines.
rules.interaction: Operates alongside the state Cartwright Act's ban on common pricing algorithms, adding city-specific penalties and a private right of action.
rules.quoted_span:
It is unlawful for a person to sell, license, or otherwise provide an
algorithmic device to a landlord.
(b) It is unlawful for a landlord to use an algorithmic device to set rental rates
or occupancy levels for residential rental property.
rules.conflict_note: A draft staff report left the final passage date blank, suggesting the ordinance may still have been pending at drafting, but the same code section confirms enactment; treated as enacted since an official code citation exists.

coverage.other_unknown_factor: whether the software only reports aggregated historical/public data without recommending future rates, or is used solely for affordable housing program compliance

rules.title_es: Prohibición del uso y venta de dispositivos algorítmicos
rules.requirement_es: Los arrendadores no pueden usar software algorítmico para fijar tarifas de alquiler o niveles de ocupación en propiedades de alquiler residencial, y nadie puede vender o proporcionar tales dispositivos algorítmicos a los arrendadores. Los inquilinos pueden demandar por daños, medidas cautelares o sanciones civiles de hasta $1,000 por infracción.
rules.key_value_es: Hasta $1,000 por infracción

rules.title: Annual Allowable Rent Increase 2026-2027

rules.title: San Francisco Just Cause Eviction Requirements
rules.requirement: A landlord in San Francisco may only evict a tenant from a covered rental unit if one of 17 specific 'just cause' reasons applies, such as nonpayment of rent, owner move-in, demolition, or Ellis Act withdrawal.

rules.title: Santa Ana Rent Stabilization Ordinance
rules.requirement: Landlords in Santa Ana cannot raise rent by more than 3% per year, or 80% of the CPI change if that is lower. If CPI is negative, no increase is allowed at all.

rules.title: Initiative Petition 25-21: An Initiative Petition to Protect Tenants by Limiting Rent Increases
rules.requirement: A proposed statewide ballot initiative would have capped annual rent increases for most residential rental units at the lesser of CPI or 5%, with exemptions for small owner-occupied buildings, new construction, certain subsidized units, short-term rentals, and nonprofit/religious facilities. The Massachusetts Supreme Judicial Court ruled the petition unconstitutional and blocked it from the November 2026 ballot because its religious-facility exemption violated Article 48's bar on initiatives relating to religion.
rules.key_value: lesser of CPI or 5%
rules.coverage_conditions: Most residential rental units statewide, subject to listed exemptions
rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied buildings with four or fewer units; newly constructed units less than 10 years old; certain publicly regulated units; short-term rentals; dwelling units in facilities operated solely for educational, religious, or nonprofit purposes
rules.interaction: Would have repealed/superseded the state's general prohibition on rent control (M.G.L. c.40P) had it passed and been enacted.

rules.key_value_es: el menor entre IPC o 5%

rules.title: Notice to Quit for Nonpayment of Rent
rules.requirement: If a tenant fails to pay rent, the landlord must give at least 14 days' written notice to quit before the lease can be terminated, unless the tenant pays or tenders all rent due with interest and costs before the answer is due in court.
rules.key_value: 14 days' notice
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to written leases where tenant has neglected or refused to pay rent due.
rules.exemptions: If the nonpayment was caused by delay in a government subsistence or rental payment, the court must continue the hearing and may treat the tenancy as not terminated if rent is later tendered.
rules.interaction: Boston's Housing Stability Notification Act imposes additional notice and reporting requirements on top of this state notice-to-quit period.
rules.quoted_span: Upon the neglect or refusal to pay the rent due under a written lease, fourteen days' notice to quit, given in writing by the landlord to the tenant, shall be sufficient to determine the lease, unless the tenant, on or before the day the answer is due, in an action by the landlord to recover possession of the premises, pays or tenders to the landlord or to his attorney all rent then due, with interest and costs of suit.
rules.title_es: Aviso de desalojo por falta de pago de renta
rules.requirement_es: Si un inquilino no paga la renta, el arrendador debe dar al menos 14 días de aviso por escrito para desalojar antes de que se pueda terminar el contrato, a menos que el inquilino pague o ofrezca toda la renta adeudada con intereses y costos antes de la fecha límite para responder en la corte.
rules.key_value_es: 14 días de aviso

rules.title: Security Deposit and Last Month's Rent Limits
rules.requirement: A landlord cannot require a tenant to pay more than first month's rent, last month's rent, a security deposit equal to one month's rent, and the cost of a key/lock at the start of a tenancy. Security deposits must be held in a separate interest-bearing account, with interest paid to the tenant, and returned within 30 days of move-out with an itemized list of any deductions.

rules.title: Real estate brokers and salesmen; persons finding dwelling accommodations for fee; contracts; payment of fee
rules.requirement: A broker fee for finding a rental home can only be charged to the person who actually hired the broker (either the landlord or the tenant), not automatically passed on to the tenant.

rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to any licensed real estate broker or salesperson finding dwelling accommodations for a fee for prospective tenants or landlords.

rules.title_es: Agentes y corredores de bienes raíces; personas que buscan alojamiento por una tarifa; contratos; pago de la tarifa

rules.key_value_es: La tarifa la paga solo la parte que contrató al corredor

rules.title: Massachusetts Security Deposit Law - Limitation on Pre-Tenancy Charges
rules.requirement: Landlords in Massachusetts cannot charge application fees, pet fees, cleaning fees, or any other upfront charges; before a tenancy begins they may only require payment of first month's rent, last month's rent, a security deposit, and a lock-change fee. Licensed real estate brokers, however, are allowed to charge separate application or screening fees.
rules.key_value: No landlord application fee allowed; only first, last, security deposit, and lock-change fee permitted
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to all residential landlords (lessors) in Massachusetts prior to the start of a tenancy; does not apply to licensed brokers acting in a bona fide separate business capacity.
rules.exemptions: Licensed real estate brokers may charge application/screening fees under 254 C.M.R. 7, provided they comply with disclosure requirements.
rules.interaction: Distinct from the broker-fee allocation statute (c.112 §87DDD 1/2); limits pre-tenancy charges generally to first/last month, deposit, and lock fee.
rules.conflict_note: The article states the law 'has been in effect since the 1970s' but gives no precise enactment or effective date; no specific date is provided in the text.

coverage.other_unknown_factor: whether the person collecting the fee is a licensed real estate broker rather than the landlord

rules.title_es: Ley de depósito de seguridad de Massachusetts - Limitación de cargos previos al arrendamiento

Sin embargo, los corredores de bienes raíces con licencia pueden cobrar tarifas separadas de solicitud o investigación.

rules.title: Prohibition on Discrimination Against Recipients of Public Assistance or Housing Subsidies
rules.requirement: Landlords and others providing rental housing or credit cannot refuse to rent to, or otherwise discriminate against, a tenant because they receive public assistance (including medical assistance) or a housing subsidy such as a Section 8 voucher or rental assistance.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to any person furnishing credit, services, or rental accommodations.
rules.interaction: Local ordinances (e.g., Boston, Cambridge) impose parallel/additional source-of-income protections on top of this statewide floor.
rules.quoted_span: For any person furnishing credit, services or rental accommodations to discriminate against any individual who is a recipient of federal, state, or local public assistance, including medical assistance, or who is a tenant receiving federal, state, or local housing subsidies, including rental assistance or rental supplements, because the individual is such a recipient, or because of any requirement of such public assistance, rental assistance, or housing subsidy program.
rules.title_es: Prohibición de discriminación contra receptores de asistencia pública o subsidios de vivienda
rules.requirement_es: Los arrendadores y otras personas que ofrecen vivienda de alquiler o crédito no pueden negarse a alquilar a un inquilino, ni discriminar de otro modo, porque reciba asistencia pública (incluida la asistencia médica) o un subsidio de vivienda como un vale de la Sección 8 o asistencia de alquiler.
