rules.conflict_note: A similar companion bill (S.2983) is pending in the Senate on the same subject; which version, if any, will be enacted is uncertain.
rules.title_es: Una ley para prevenir la fijación algorítmica de rentas (FAIR Act)
rules.requirement_es: Este proyecto de ley restringiría el uso de software o dispositivos algorítmicos para fijar o coordinar los precios de la vivienda de alquiler, pero aún no ha sido aprobado; todavía está pendiente en comité.

rules.title: An Act prohibiting algorithmic rent setting
rules.requirement: This bill would prohibit the use of algorithmic devices to set rental prices for housing in Massachusetts.
rules.coverage_conditions: Not specified in chunk.
rules.quoted_span: An Act prohibiting algorithmic rent setting
rules.conflict_note: A similar companion bill (H.5222) is pending in the House on the same subject; which version, if any, will be enacted is uncertain.
rules.title_es: Una ley que prohíbe la fijación algorítmica de rentas
rules.requirement_es: Este proyecto de ley prohibiría el uso de dispositivos algorítmicos para fijar los precios de alquiler de vivienda en Massachusetts.

rules.title: An Act petition for a special law authorizing the city of Boston to implement rent stabilization and tenant eviction protections
rules.requirement: This bill would have authorized the city of Boston to create its own rent stabilization program, but the bill was not enacted and was instead accompanied by a study order, effectively ending its progress in this session.
rules.coverage_conditions: Would have applied to rental housing within the city of Boston if enacted.
rules.interaction: Would have authorized Boston to adopt local rent stabilization notwithstanding the state's general prohibition on rent control (M.G.L. c.40P); did not pass.
rules.quoted_span: An Act petition for a special law authorizing the city of Boston to implement rent stabilization and tenant eviction protections
rules.conflict_note: Bill did not pass; final legislative action was 'Accompanied a study order' indicating it was shelved rather than enacted or formally voted down.
rules.title_es: Petición de ley especial para autorizar a la ciudad de Boston a implementar estabilización de renta y protecciones de desalojo
rules.requirement_es: Este proyecto de ley habría autorizado a la ciudad de Boston a crear su propio programa de estabilización de renta, pero el proyecto no fue aprobado y en su lugar se acompañó de una orden de estudio, lo que efectivamente puso fin a su avance en esta sesión.

rules.title: Housing Stability Notification Act (HSNA)
rules.requirement: Landlords and foreclosing owners in Boston must give tenants a Notice of Tenants' Rights and Resources at the same time they serve a Notice to Quit or a Notice of Non-renewal of lease, and must send a copy of that notice along with a Certificate of Compliance/Service to the City's Office of Housing Stability.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to all landlords/foreclosing owners intending to end a tenancy or post-foreclosure occupancy of a unit in the City of Boston.
rules.exemptions: Residences in any hospital, skilled nursing facility or health facility; and residences in a non-profit facility whose primary purpose is providing short-term treatment, assistance or therapy for alcohol, drug, or other substance abuse.
rules.interaction: Imposes notice and city-reporting requirements that apply in addition to the state notice-to-quit requirement under M.G.L. c.186 §11.
rules.quoted_span:
The Ordinance applies to all landlords/foreclosing owners intending to end a
tenancy or post-foreclosure occupancy of a unit in the City of Boston.

coverage.other_unknown_factor: whether the property is a hospital, skilled nursing facility, health facility, or a non-profit facility primarily providing short-term substance abuse treatment

rules.effective_date_note: New notification ordinance enactment
rules.title_es: Ley de Notificación de Estabilidad de Vivienda (HSNA)
rules.requirement_es: Los arrendadores y propietarios que ejecutan una ejecución hipotecaria en Boston deben entregar a los inquilinos un Aviso de Derechos y Recursos del Inquilino al mismo tiempo que sirven un Aviso de Desalojo o un Aviso de No Renovación del contrato, y deben enviar una copia de ese aviso junto con un Certificado de Cumplimiento/Servicio a la Oficina de Estabilidad de Vivienda de la Ciudad.

rules.title: An Act petition for a special law authorizing the city of Boston to implement rent stabilization and tenant eviction protections
rules.requirement: This bill would have authorized the city of Boston to adopt tenant eviction protections (just-cause style rules), but it was not enacted and was instead accompanied by a study order.
rules.coverage_conditions: Would have applied to rental housing within the city of Boston if enacted.
rules.interaction: Would have authorized Boston to adopt local just-cause/tenant eviction protections; did not pass.
rules.quoted_span: that the city of Boston be authorized to implement rent stabilization and tenant eviction protections.
rules.conflict_note: Bill did not pass; final legislative action was 'Accompanied a study order' indicating it was shelved rather than enacted or formally voted down.
rules.title_es: Petición de ley especial para autorizar a la ciudad de Boston a implementar estabilización de renta y protecciones de desalojo de inquilinos
rules.requirement_es: Este proyecto de ley habría autorizado a la ciudad de Boston a adoptar protecciones de desalojo de inquilinos (reglas de tipo causa justa), pero no fue aprobado y en su lugar se acompañó de una orden de estudio.

rules.title: Boston Fair Chance Tenant Selection Policy
rules.requirement: Covered housing providers may not use blanket bans against applicants with arrests or convictions; they must consider criminal history case-by-case, excluding arrests without conviction, convictions subject to judicial relief, juvenile records, and convictions older than 5 years (with limited safety exceptions). Providers also may not use an applicant's credit score alone to approve or deny housing.
rules.key_value: 5-year conviction lookback limit; no blanket criminal bans; no credit-score-based denial
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to housing providers receiving DND funding and/or land, or that have income-restricted units created under the BPDA Inclusionary Development Policy.
rules.exemptions: Does not apply where a direct relationship exists between a conviction and the housing sought or an unreasonable risk of harm to others; does not apply to current criminal behavior; federal or state law requirements preempt the policy where conflicting.
rules.interaction: Applies only to DND-funded/income-restricted housing; broader market-rate screening is governed by state anti-discrimination law.
rules.citation: Boston Fair Chance Tenant Selection Policy (DND, Feb. 2017)
rules.quoted_span:
Housing providers receiving Department of Neighborhood Development (DND) funding and/or 
land, or that have income restricted units created under the Boston Planning and Development 
Agency (BPDA) Inclusionary Development Policy will not impose a blanket policy that denies 
housing to anyone with arrests and or convictions.
rules.conflict_note: This is a city policy applicable only to subsidized/income-restricted or DND-funded housing providers, not to general market-rate multifamily buildings; state/federal screening law provides broader but less detailed protections.

coverage.other_unknown_factor: whether the housing provider receives DND funding/land or has BPDA inclusionary income-restricted units

rules.effective_date_note: New policy establishing fair chance tenant selection requirements
rules.title_es: Política de Selección de Inquilinos de Oportunidad Justa de Boston
rules.requirement_es: Los proveedores de vivienda cubiertos no pueden usar rechazos generales contra solicitantes con arrestos o condenas; deben considerar los antecedentes penales caso por caso, excluyendo los arrestos sin condena, las condenas sujetas a alivio judicial, los registros juveniles y las condenas de más de 5 años de antigüedad (con excepciones limitadas de seguridad). Los proveedores tampoco pueden usar únicamente el puntaje crediticio de un solicitante para aprobar o negar la vivienda.
rules.key_value_es: Límite de revisión de condenas de 5 años; no se permiten rechazos generales por antecedentes penales; no se permite negación basada únicamente en el puntaje crediticio

rules.title: Boston Fair Housing Regulations - Source of Income Protection
rules.requirement: Landlords in Boston cannot refuse to rent to tenants because they use rental assistance, including Section 8 vouchers, disability vouchers, or veterans vouchers.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to housing rentals, sales, and financing within the City of Boston.
rules.interaction: Complements the state source-of-income/public-assistance discrimination protection under M.G.L. c.151B §4(10).
rules.citation: Boston Fair Housing Regulations - Source of Income Protection
rules.quoted_span:
The landlord tells you they don't accept rental assistance. This includes Section
8 vouchers, social security disability vouchers, and veterans vouchers.
rules.title_es: Reglamentos de Vivienda Justa de Boston - Protección por fuente de ingresos
rules.requirement_es: Los arrendadores en Boston no pueden negarse a alquilar a inquilinos porque utilicen asistencia de alquiler, incluidos los vales de la Sección 8, vales por discapacidad o vales para veteranos.

rules.title: Cambridge Fair Housing Ordinance
rules.requirement: Landlords, sellers and rental agents in Cambridge may not discriminate against housing applicants based on source of income, including Section 8 vouchers and other public benefits, among other protected categories.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to rental housing transactions in Cambridge, including viewing or renting an apartment and terms and conditions of tenancy; exemption for 2-family dwellings when the owner lives there.
rules.exemptions: 2-family dwellings, when the owner lives there
rules.interaction: Parallels the state source-of-income/public-assistance protection under M.G.L. c.151B §4(10).
rules.quoted_span: Source of Income, includes Section 8 and public benefits
rules.title_es: Ordenanza de Vivienda Justa de Cambridge
rules.requirement_es: Los arrendadores, vendedores y agentes de alquiler en Cambridge no pueden discriminar a los solicitantes de vivienda según la fuente de ingresos, incluidos los vales de la Sección 8 y otros beneficios públicos, entre otras categorías protegidas.

rules.title: Anti-Eviction Act – Notice and Unconscionable Rent Increase Standard
rules.requirement: A landlord can only raise rent by terminating the old lease and offering a new lease with the increased rent, after giving proper written notice. The increase must not be 'unconscionable' (so unreasonable as to shock the conscience) and must comply with any local rent control ordinance.
rules.key_value: Must not be 'unconscionable'; no fixed numeric cap
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to residential tenancies statewide where a landlord seeks to raise rent via lease termination/renewal.
rules.interaction: State law requires rent increases not be 'unconscionable' and must comply with any local rent control ordinance; local caps govern where they exist.
rules.quoted_span:
The increase in rent must not be 
unconscionable; it must not be so unreasonable as to shock the conscience of a fair and honest 
person and must comply with any municipal ordinances governing rent increases.
rules.conflict_note: State law sets only a vague 'unconscionable' standard and explicitly defers to municipal rent control ordinances where they exist, so numeric caps come from local law.
rules.title_es: Ley Contra el Desalojo - Aviso y norma de aumento de renta injustificado
rules.requirement_es: Un arrendador solo puede aumentar la renta terminando el contrato anterior y ofreciendo uno nuevo con la renta aumentada, después de dar el aviso por escrito adecuado. El aumento no debe ser 'injustificado' (es decir, tan irrazonable que resulte chocante) y debe cumplir con cualquier ordenanza local de control de renta.
rules.key_value_es: No debe ser 'injustificado'; sin tope numérico fijo

rules.title: Condominium/Cooperative Conversion Rent Increase Prohibition
rules.requirement: If a building is converted to condominium, cooperative, or fee-simple ownership, landlords cannot raise rents to cover costs resulting solely from the conversion, though increases for new services or amenities are still allowed.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to all tenants in a building undergoing conversion to condominium, cooperative, or fee-simple ownership of units, regardless of protected tenancy status.
rules.quoted_span:
If a building is converted to a condominium or cooperative form of ownership, or to fee 
simple ownership of units, rents may not be increased to cover cos ts resulting solely from the 
conversion (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.31).

coverage.other_unknown_factor: whether the building has undergone or is undergoing conversion to condominium/cooperative/fee-simple ownership

rules.title_es: Prohibición de aumento de renta por conversión a condominio/cooperativa
rules.requirement_es: Si un edificio se convierte en condominio, cooperativa o propiedad plena, los arrendadores no pueden aumentar las rentas para cubrir costos que resulten únicamente de la conversión, aunque los aumentos por nuevos servicios o comodidades sí están permitidos.

rules.title: Newly Constructed Multiple Dwellings Law – 30-Year Rent Control Exemption
rules.requirement: Newly constructed multi-family dwellings are exempt from any local rent control ordinance for 30 years after completion of construction; rents subsidized by government funding may also be exempt from local rent control.
rules.key_value: 30-year exemption from local rent control
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to newly constructed multiple dwellings statewide, overriding municipal rent control ordinances.
rules.exemptions: Subsidized/government-funded rents may also be exempt from local rent control.
rules.interaction: Overrides/limits local rent control ordinances by exempting newly constructed buildings for 30 years after completion.
rules.quoted_span:
Under the Newly Constructed Multiple Dwellings Law ( N.J.S.A. 2A:42 -84.5), newly 
constructed multiple dwellings shall be exempt from any local rent control ordinances for a period 
of 30 years following completion of construction of the building.
rules.conflict_note: This state law exempts newly constructed multi-family buildings from local rent control ordinances for 30 years, overriding municipal rent control for qualifying units.

coverage.other_unknown_factor: whether the rent is subsidized by governmental funding (which may also exempt it from local rent control)

rules.title_es: Ley de viviendas múltiples de nueva construcción - Exención de control de renta por 30 años
rules.requirement_es: Las viviendas multifamiliares de nueva construcción están exentas de cualquier ordenanza local de control de renta durante 30 años después de completarse la construcción; las rentas subsidiadas con fondos gubernamentales también pueden estar exentas del control de renta local.
rules.key_value_es: Exención de 30 años del control de renta local

rules.title: New Jersey Anti-Eviction Act
rules.requirement: A landlord may only evict a residential tenant for one of the specific statutory good-cause reasons (such as nonpayment of rent, disorderly conduct, property damage, lease violations, or removal from the rental market), and in most cases must first serve a required notice (Notice to Cease and/or Notice to Quit) before filing suit.
rules.key_value: Good cause required; notice periods range from 3 days to 3 months depending on cause
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to most residential rental properties including single-family homes, mobile homes and land in a mobile home park, apartment buildings and complexes, and rooming and boarding homes.
rules.exemptions: Does not apply to two- or three-unit owner-occupied premises with two or fewer rental units; does not apply to hotel, motel, or guest house occupants who are transient or seasonal guests (unless they have no alternate residence and reside there continually); does not apply to a unit held in trust for a developmentally disabled immediate family member who permanently occupies the unit.
rules.quoted_span:
A landlord must have 
good cause to evict a tenant (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-53).

coverage.other_unknown_factor: whether a unit is held in trust for and permanently occupied by a developmentally disabled immediate family member, or is used for transient/seasonal hotel, motel, or guest house occupancy

rules.title_es: Ley Contra el Desalojo de Nueva Jersey
rules.requirement_es: Un arrendador solo puede desalojar a un inquilino residencial por uno de los motivos de causa justa específicos establecidos por ley (como falta de pago de renta, conducta desordenada, daño a la propiedad, violaciones del contrato, o retiro del mercado de alquiler), y en la mayoría de los casos debe dar primero el aviso requerido (Aviso de Cese y/o Aviso de Desalojo) antes de presentar la demanda.
rules.key_value_es: Se requiere causa justa; los períodos de aviso varían de 3 días a 3 meses según el motivo

rules.title: Senior Citizens and Disabled Protected Tenancy Act
rules.requirement: Eligible senior citizens, permanently disabled tenants, or qualifying disabled veterans living in a building being converted to a condominium, cooperative, or fee-simple ownership may be protected from eviction for up to 40 years, provided their family income does not exceed a set threshold.
rules.key_value: Up to 40 years of eviction protection; income cap = 3x county average per-person income or $50,000, whichever is greater
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to buildings undergoing condominium, cooperative, or fee-simple conversion where qualifying tenants (62+, permanently disabled, or qualifying disabled veteran) have resided at least one year prior to the conversion recording date and meet an income threshold.
rules.quoted_span:
Tenants may be protected from eviction for 40 years 
if their family income is not more than three (3) times the average per person income in their 
county or $50,000.00, whichever  is greater (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.28).
rules.conflict_note: An amendment (Tenant Protection Act of 1992) extends similar protections to additional tenants in Hudson County who did not otherwise qualify, but the text does not attribute this to a specific city, so it is not separately recorded.

coverage.other_unknown_factor: whether the building is undergoing condominium/cooperative/fee-simple conversion, and whether the tenant qualifies by age, disability, veteran status, tenancy duration, and income

rules.title_es: Ley de Arrendamiento Protegido para Adultos Mayores y Personas con Discapacidad
rules.requirement_es: Los adultos mayores elegibles, los inquilinos con discapacidad permanente o los veteranos con discapacidad que califiquen y vivan en un edificio que se esté convirtiendo en condominio, cooperativa o propiedad plena pueden estar protegidos contra el desalojo hasta por 40 años, siempre que el ingreso familiar no exceda un umbral establecido.
rules.key_value_es: Hasta 40 años de protección contra el desalojo; tope de ingresos = 3 veces el ingreso promedio por persona del condado o $50,000, lo que sea mayor

rules.title: Reprisal / Anti-Retaliation Protection for Tenants
rules.requirement: A landlord cannot evict, substantially change lease terms, or refuse to renew a lease in retaliation for a tenant exercising certain civil rights, such as enforcing lease or legal rights, complaining to authorities about code violations, or participating in a tenant organization.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to all rental properties used for dwelling purposes, including mobile homes.
rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings are excluded from this anti-reprisal protection.
rules.quoted_span:
A landlord cannot take reprisal action against a tenant by eviction, substantial alteration of 
a lease or its terms, or refusal to renew a lease when a tenant exercises certain civil rights (N.J.S.A. 
2A:42-10.10).
rules.title_es: Protección contra represalias / antirrepresalias para inquilinos
rules.requirement_es: Un arrendador no puede desalojar, cambiar sustancialmente los términos del contrato, ni negarse a renovar un contrato como represalia por el ejercicio de ciertos derechos civiles por parte del inquilino, como hacer valer derechos legales o del contrato, quejarse a las autoridades sobre violaciones de códigos, o participar en una organización de inquilinos.

rules.title: Foreclosure Fairness Act - Notice and Eviction Protections for Tenants in Foreclosed Properties
rules.requirement: Foreclosure alone is not grounds for eviction; a tenant in a foreclosed property generally keeps their tenancy. If a buyer who wants to personally occupy the property as a primary residence purchases it, the landlord must give the tenant a 90-day notice to quit, and new owners must notify tenants in English and Spanish that they are not required to move.
rules.key_value: 90-day notice to quit (owner-occupant purchaser)
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to residential rental units in properties that have been foreclosed upon; notice posting method varies by building size (10 or fewer units vs. more than 10 units).
rules.exemptions: Month-to-month tenants and two- and three-family owner-occupied units are NOT exempt from the 90-day notice requirement (i.e., no exemption applies to them).
rules.quoted_span:
Before a tenant can be evicted due 
to foreclosure, the landlord must provide the tenant with a 90 -day notice to qui t when the 
foreclosed property has been purchased by a buyer who wants to personally occupy it as his or her 
primary residence.
rules.conflict_note: Separate, more detailed notice procedures and posting requirements are set out at N.J.S.A. 2A:50-70(c)2 for buildings with more than 10 units, and pressure-tactic prohibitions at N.J.S.A. 2A:50-71(b); these are part of the same Foreclosure Fairness Act scheme.

coverage.other_unknown_factor: whether the new owner/purchaser intends to personally occupy the unit as a primary residence, and total number of dwelling units in the building (affects notice posting method)

rules.title_es: Ley de Equidad en Ejecuciones Hipotecarias - Protecciones de aviso y desalojo para inquilinos en propiedades ejecutadas
rules.requirement_es: La ejecución hipotecaria por sí sola no es motivo de desalojo; un inquilino en una propiedad ejecutada generalmente conserva su arrendamiento. Si un comprador que desea ocupar personalmente la propiedad como residencia principal la compra, el arrendador debe dar al inquilino un aviso de desalojo de 90 días, y los nuevos propietarios deben notificar a los inquilinos en inglés y español que no están obligados a mudarse.
rules.key_value_es: Aviso de desalojo de 90 días (comprador que ocupará la propiedad)

rules.title: New Jersey Security Deposit Law
rules.requirement: A landlord who collects a security deposit cannot require more than one and one-half times one month's rent, and increases to the deposit are capped. Interest earned on the deposit belongs to the tenant and the deposit must generally be returned within 30 days after the tenancy ends.
rules.key_value: 1.5 months' rent
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to most residential rental properties in New Jersey, including mobile homes.
rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings are exempt unless the tenant makes a written request to the landlord and 30 days pass.
rules.quoted_span:
The maximum-security deposit to be collected by the landlord cannot be more than 
one and one-half times one month’s rent ( N.J.S.A. 46:8-21.2 ).

coverage.other_unknown_factor: whether the dwelling is owner-occupied (two- or three-family)

rules.title_es: Ley de depósito de seguridad de Nueva Jersey
rules.requirement_es: Un arrendador que cobre un depósito de seguridad no puede exigir más de una vez y media la renta mensual, y los aumentos del depósito tienen un tope. El interés generado por el depósito pertenece al inquilino y el depósito generalmente debe devolverse dentro de los 30 días posteriores al fin del arrendamiento.
rules.key_value_es: 1.5 meses de renta

rules.title: Residential rental property application fee not to exceed $50
rules.requirement: Landlords or their agents cannot charge more than $50 for an application or similar fee to lease or sublease a residential rental property. The fee limit adjusts annually based on inflation.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to residential rental properties for dwelling purposes, except one-family or two-family dwellings and licensed real estate agents who are not the landlord.
rules.exemptions: Dwelling units in one-family or two-family dwellings offered for rent; licensees of the New Jersey Real Estate Commission unless they are the landlord of the property.
rules.quoted_span:
A landlord, or
agent thereof, shall not require an application or other similar fee to apply
to lease or sublease a residential rental property for dwelling purposes, which
exceeds $50.
rules.conflict_note: Section 3 states the act takes effect on the first day of the fourth month following enactment (approved January 20, 2026), which would be May 1, 2026; subsection d. separately describes an annual CPI adjustment mechanism beginning January 1 of the year following enactment (2027), which is a distinct administrative timeline, not a conflicting effective date for the core $50 cap.

coverage.other_unknown_factor: Whether the property is a one-family or two-family dwelling (exempt) rather than a larger multifamily building, and whether the landlord/agent is a licensed NJ real estate agent (exempt unless also the landlord).

rules.effective_date_note: New application fee cap law
rules.title_es: La tarifa de solicitud de propiedad de alquiler residencial no debe exceder los $50
rules.requirement_es: Los arrendadores o sus agentes no pueden cobrar más de $50 por una tarifa de solicitud o similar para arrendar o subarrendar una propiedad de alquiler residencial. El límite de la tarifa se ajusta anualmente según la inflación.

rules.title: New Jersey Law Against Discrimination - source of income and other protected classes
rules.requirement: Landlords may not refuse to rent or otherwise discriminate against prospective tenants based on protected characteristics including source of lawful income, familial status, and other listed categories.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to all landlord-tenant relationships in New Jersey.
rules.exemptions: Does not apply to two-family owner-occupied dwellings, rooms in an owner or resident-occupied single home, or residences planned exclusively for and occupied by one sex (e.g., YMCA) or age-restricted housing as it pertains to familial status.
rules.quoted_span:
The New Jersey Law Against Discrimination (LAD), 
N.J.S.A. 10:5-12(g) to -(h), prohibits discrimination when selling or renting property and requires 
equal treatment in the sale or rental of housing regardless of race, creed, color, national origin, 
ancestry, sex, marital status, civil union status, domestic partnership status, familial status, 
affectional or sexual orientation, gender  identity or expression, mental and physical disability, 
nationality, or source of lawful income.

coverage.other_unknown_factor: whether the dwelling is owner-occupied or a single-sex/age-restricted residence

rules.title_es: Ley Contra la Discriminación de Nueva Jersey - fuente de ingresos y otras clases protegidas
rules.requirement_es: Los arrendadores no pueden negarse a alquilar ni discriminar de otro modo contra inquilinos potenciales por características protegidas, incluida la fuente legal de ingresos, el estado familiar y otras categorías enumeradas.

rules.title: Fair Chance in Housing Act
rules.requirement: Landlords cannot ask about or consider an applicant's criminal record until after making a conditional offer, and even then may only consider limited categories of serious or recent convictions, not arrests, expunged records, or old low-level offenses.
rules.key_value: Criminal history inquiries barred until after conditional offer; lookback limits of 1-6 years depending on offense degree
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to rental dwelling units offered for rent by a housing provider, except owner-occupied premises of not more than four dwelling units.
rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied premises with no more than four dwelling units; certain serious convictions (murder, aggravated sexual assault, kidnapping, arson, human trafficking, sexual assault, child sexual exploitation, lifetime sex offender registrants) and drug-related meth manufacture on federally assisted housing premises may still be considered.
rules.citation: N.J.S.A. 46:8-52 et seq. (P.L.2021, c.110) - Fair Chance in Housing Act
rules.quoted_span:
A
housing provider
shall not require an applicant to
complete any housing application that includes any inquiries regarding an
applicant’s criminal record prior to the provision of a conditional offer
rules.conflict_note: Effective date computed from 'first day of the seventh month next following the date of enactment' based on the stated approval date of June 18, 2021.

coverage.other_unknown_factor: whether the premises is owner-occupied

rules.effective_date_note: New Fair Chance in Housing Act requirements
rules.title_es: Ley de Oportunidad Justa en la Vivienda
rules.requirement_es: Los arrendadores no pueden preguntar sobre ni considerar el historial penal de un solicitante hasta después de hacer una oferta condicional, y aun así solo pueden considerar categorías limitadas de condenas graves o recientes, no arrestos, registros sellados ni delitos menores antiguos.
rules.key_value_es: Las preguntas sobre antecedentes penales están prohibidas hasta después de la oferta condicional; límites de revisión de 1 a 6 años según el grado del delito

rules.title: Forbidding the Algorithmic Inflation of Rent (FAIR) Act
rules.requirement: New Jersey law makes it illegal for landlords to use algorithmic devices, software, or coordinators that pool competitively sensitive rental data (like prices, lease terms, or occupancy levels) across multiple property owners to set or recommend rental prices, lease terms, or occupancy levels. It also bans landlords from engaging in tacit or express 'parallel pricing coordination' to raise or manipulate rents.
rules.key_value: Ban on algorithmic rent-setting / coordinated pricing among landlords
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to any rental property owner (person owning one or more residential dwelling units) and any coordinator providing algorithmic revenue management software or similar devices used to perform a 'coordinating function' for multiple rental property owners.
rules.exemptions: Does not apply to government entities setting rents via affordability controls, spreadsheets without AI requiring human analysis, databases that only query unprocessed data, real estate brokerage databases that don't set/recommend prices, or information used solely for research/statistics/testing or free public rent estimates.
rules.interaction: May preempt stricter or differing local algorithmic pricing ordinances once effective.
rules.quoted_span:
This act shall take effect on the first day of
the twelfth month next following the date of enactment.
rules.conflict_note: The act's provision barring conflicting municipal ordinances may preempt existing local algorithmic rent-setting bans (e.g., Hoboken, Jersey City) once effective.

coverage.other_unknown_factor: whether the rental property owner or coordinator uses an algorithmic device, software, or coordinating function involving competitively sensitive data shared across multiple owners

rules.effective_date_note: New algorithmic rent-setting ban
rules.title_es: Ley para Prohibir la Inflación Algorítmica de la Renta (FAIR Act)
rules.requirement_es: La ley de Nueva Jersey hace ilegal que los arrendadores usen dispositivos algorítmicos, software o coordinadores que agrupen datos de alquiler competitivamente sensibles (como precios, términos de arrendamiento o niveles de ocupación) entre múltiples propietarios para fijar o recomendar precios de alquiler, términos de arrendamiento o niveles de ocupación. También prohíbe que los arrendadores participen en 'coordinación de precios paralela' tácita o expresa para aumentar o manipular las rentas.
rules.key_value_es: Prohibición de fijación algorítmica de renta / coordinación de precios entre arrendadores

rules.title: Hoboken Rent Control - Base Rent and Annual CPI Increase Cap
rules.requirement: Landlords may only raise rent at lease expiration or termination of a periodic lease, and the annual increase is capped at 5% or the CPI percentage difference, whichever is less. Increases above this cap are void and must be refunded to the tenant.
rules.key_value: 5% or CPI differential, whichever is less
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to dwellings subject to Hoboken Rent Control chapter, with base rent set as of October 1, 1985.
rules.interaction: Governs over state rule r-0043 where it covers the unit.
rules.citation: Hoboken Code ch. 155, Art. II / ch. 158
rules.quoted_span: At the expiration of a lease or at the termination of a lease of a periodic tenant, no landlord may request or receive a percentage increase in rent which is greater than 5% or the percentage difference between the consumer price index three months prior to the expiration or termination of the lease and three months prior to the commencement of the lease term, whichever is less.
rules.conflict_note: Ordinance has been amended multiple times (2011, 2023, 2025); surcharge, hardship-increase, and disclosure provisions are codified in related chapters with differing effective dates.

coverage.other_unknown_factor: whether the dwelling is subject to this chapter (rent-controlled status, vacancy decontrol history)

rules.effective_date_note: Original establishment of Hoboken rent control cap
rules.title_es: Control de renta en Hoboken - Renta base y tope de aumento anual por IPC
rules.requirement_es: Los arrendadores solo pueden aumentar la renta al vencimiento del contrato o al terminar un arrendamiento periódico, y el aumento anual tiene un tope del 5% o la diferencia porcentual del IPC, lo que sea menor. Los aumentos por encima de este tope son nulos y deben reembolsarse al inquilino.
rules.key_value_es: 5% o diferencial del IPC, lo que sea menor

rules.title: Ban on Algorithmic Price Fixing for Residential Rentals
rules.requirement: Landlords renting residential dwelling units in Hoboken are prohibited from using software, algorithms, or data-sharing platforms to collect and analyze nonpublic competitor information in order to coordinate, recommend, or implement rental prices, lease terms, or occupancy levels among competing landlords.
rules.key_value: Prohibition on algorithmic price fixing using nonpublic competitor data
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to landlords renting any residential dwelling unit (primary residence) in the City of Hoboken, excluding medical/long-term care or detention facilities.
rules.exemptions: Medical/long-term care or detention facilities are excluded from the definition of residential dwelling unit.
rules.interaction: State FAIR Act may preempt or overlap with this local ban depending on its conflicting-ordinance provisions.
rules.quoted_span: Landlords who rent any residential dwelling unit (defined as any primary residence excluding medical/long-term care or detention facilities) in the City of Hoboken are prohibited from price fixing using algorithmic pricing.
rules.conflict_note: May interact with or be preempted by the state FAIR Act (P.L.2026, c.43) once effective.
rules.effective_date_note: New first-ever algorithmic price fixing ban
rules.title_es: Prohibición de fijación algorítmica de precios para alquileres residenciales
rules.requirement_es: Los arrendadores que alquilan unidades residenciales en Hoboken tienen prohibido usar software, algoritmos o plataformas para compartir datos con el fin de recopilar y analizar información no pública de competidores para coordinar, recomendar o implementar precios de alquiler, términos de arrendamiento o niveles de ocupación entre arrendadores competidores.
rules.key_value_es: Prohibición de fijación algorítmica de precios usando datos no públicos de competidores

rules.title: Jersey City Rent Control Ordinance
rules.requirement: Jersey City regulates how much landlords may increase rent on most rental units through its Rent Control Ordinance, administered by the Office of Landlord/Tenant Relations. Buildings with 1-4 units are exempt from rent control, and other exemptions may apply upon owner request.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to rental properties in Jersey City with 5 or more units; properties of 1-4 units are exempt. Other exemptions available upon application review.
rules.exemptions: All 1-4 unit properties are exempt from rent control; additional exemptions available via Rent Control Exemption Request (e.g., capital improvement, hardship, vacancy applications).
rules.interaction: Governs over state rule r-0043 where it covers the unit.
rules.quoted_span:
The Office of Landlord Tenant Relations administers and enforces the
Rent Control Ordinance, Chapter 260
of the Jersey City Municipal Code and provides education, information and referrals to city residents in connection with landlord/tenant issues.
rules.conflict_note: The specific rent increase cap/formula is not stated in this document; only the existence of the ordinance and the 1-4 unit exemption are described.

coverage.other_unknown_factor: whether the owner has been granted a Rent Control Exemption (e.g., capital improvement, hardship, or vacancy exemption)

rules.title_es: Ordenanza de Control de Renta de Jersey City
rules.requirement_es: Jersey City regula cuánto pueden aumentar la renta los arrendadores en la mayoría de las unidades de alquiler a través de su Ordenanza de Control de Renta, administrada por la Oficina de Relaciones entre Propietarios e Inquilinos. Los edificios de 1 a 4 unidades están exentos del control de renta, y pueden aplicar otras exenciones a solicitud del propietario.

rules.title: Jersey City Code § 218-12 - Algorithmic Rent Coordination Prohibition
rules.requirement: Landlords in Jersey City are prohibited from using algorithmic rent coordination services to set or recommend rents. Violations can be enforced through both city enforcement and private lawsuits, with fines up to $2,000 per day.
rules.key_value: up to $2,000 per day
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to landlords using algorithmic rent coordination services in Jersey City.
rules.interaction: State FAIR Act may preempt or overlap with this local ordinance; relationship not yet settled.
rules.quoted_span:
Jersey City Code § 218-12 (effective June 2025)
Prohibits a landlord’s use of algorithmic rent coordination services; includes public and private enforcement; fines up to $2,000 per day.
rules.conflict_note: May be preempted or superseded by the state FAIR Act (P.L.2026, c.43) once it takes effect.

Las infracciones pueden hacerse cumplir tanto mediante la aplicación de la ley de la ciudad como mediante demandas privadas, con multas de hasta $2,000 por día.

rules.title: Newark Rent Control Ordinance - Annual Rent Increase Limit
rules.requirement: Landlords in Newark may not raise rent at lease renewal or periodic tenancy termination by more than the percentage change in the Consumer Price Index over a specified period, and in no case may the increase exceed 4% in any 12-month period.
rules.key_value: CPI-based increase, capped at 4%
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to all multiple dwellings as defined in the ordinance (buildings containing one or more apartments rented or offered for rent), unless exempt under the chapter's exemption list.
rules.exemptions: Public housing; motel/hotel space rented day-to-day to transients; commercial space; newly constructed multiple dwellings and vacant dwellings (per §§19:2-18.1 and 19:2-18.2); units rehabilitated under Federal/State Rental Rehabilitation Programs receiving Section 8 subsidies (exempt only during subsidy tenure); units subject to a governmental agency rent-regulation contract that supersedes city authority.
rules.interaction: Governs over state rule r-0043 where it covers the unit.
rules.quoted_span: At the expiration of a lease or at the termination of the lease of a periodic tenant, no landlord may request or receive an increase greater than the percentage increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) from the CPI 15 months prior to the month of the proposed rent increase to the CPI three months prior to the month of the proposed rent increase. In no case shall the allowable rent increase exceed 4%.
rules.conflict_note: Ordinance has been amended multiple times (2017, 2024, 2026); exact current effective date of the base CPI/4% cap provision is not precisely stated across sources.

coverage.other_unknown_factor: whether the dwelling is a newly constructed multiple dwelling or vacant dwelling exempt under §§19:2-18.1/19:2-18.2, or is subject to a Section 8/Rental Rehabilitation subsidy or a government rent-regulation contract

rules.title_es: Ordenanza de Control de Renta de Newark - Límite de aumento anual de renta
rules.requirement_es: Los arrendadores en Newark no pueden aumentar la renta al renovar el contrato o al terminar un arrendamiento periódico más del cambio porcentual del Índice de Precios al Consumidor durante un período especificado, y en ningún caso el aumento puede exceder el 4% en cualquier período de 12 meses.
rules.key_value_es: Aumento basado en el IPC, con tope del 4%

rules.title: Anti-Displacement / Unconscionable Rent Provisions
rules.requirement: Newark law prohibits landlords from imposing rent increases that are 'unconscionable'—i.e., exceedingly harsh or unreasonable increases that exceed the landlord's rising expenses and are not comparable to rents at similar properties; such increases can constitute unlawful tenant displacement.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to residential rental properties including market-rate and unsubsidized units; for properties under a redevelopment or financial agreement, rent exceeding the approved pro-forma is automatically considered unconscionable.
rules.exemptions: Units statutorily exempt from Rent Control under N.J.S.A. 2A:42-84.1-84.6, and units controlled/governed by HUD.
rules.interaction: Governs over state rule r-0043 where it covers the unit.
rules.quoted_span: Shall mean any rental increase for residential properties including but not limited to market and unsubsidized units, whose rental increases are exceedingly harsh or unreasonable that exceed the increase in the landlord’s expenses; and is not comparable to rents charged at similar properties.
rules.conflict_note: Section number not stated in this chunk; citation inferred from ordinance numbers referenced in the text (6PSF-C, 6PSF-H).

coverage.other_unknown_factor: whether the unit is statutorily exempt from Rent Control or controlled by HUD

rules.title_es: Disposiciones contra el desplazamiento / renta injustificada
rules.requirement_es: La ley de Newark prohíbe que los arrendadores impongan aumentos de renta 'injustificados', es decir, aumentos excesivamente severos o irrazonables que excedan el aumento de los gastos del arrendador y que no sean comparables a las rentas de propiedades similares; tales aumentos pueden constituir un desplazamiento ilegal de inquilinos.

rules.title: Ban the Box - Rental Housing Criminal History Restrictions
rules.requirement: Landlords and real estate brokers may not inquire into or consider an applicant's criminal history until after a formal rental application is submitted, must provide notice before conducting a criminal background check, and are limited in how far back and what kinds of convictions they may consider.
rules.key_value: 8 years (indictable offenses); 5 years (disorderly persons/municipal violations)
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to landlords and real estate brokers renting, leasing, or subleasing real property in Newark.
rules.exemptions: Does not apply to rental of a single unit in a two-family dwelling where the owner occupies the other unit, or to a room/rooms rented by an owner-occupant of a one-family dwelling; also exempt where federal/state law requires/permits consideration of criminal history, and for properties designated for programs encouraging housing for individuals with criminal histories.
rules.quoted_span: Inquiry into and consideration of any applicant's criminal history shall take place only after the applicant has submitted a formal application.

coverage.other_unknown_factor: whether the owner occupies the other unit in a two-family dwelling, or rents rooms in an owner-occupied one-family dwelling

rules.effective_date_note: New ban-the-box criminal history ordinance
rules.title_es: Ban the Box - Restricciones sobre antecedentes penales en vivienda de alquiler
rules.requirement_es: Los arrendadores y corredores de bienes raíces no pueden indagar sobre ni considerar el historial penal de un solicitante hasta después de que se presente una solicitud formal de alquiler, deben dar aviso antes de realizar una verificación de antecedentes penales, y están limitados en cuánto tiempo atrás y qué tipos de condenas pueden considerar.
rules.key_value_es: 8 años (delitos graves/indictables); 5 años (infracciones menores/violaciones municipales)
